summary: A simpler Auto-EQ fitter (fixed band grid, gains only) fits the intended tone curve more closely on average but fails the predefined rule on 56 of 2084 cases, so the current fitter stays.

candidate.layout: low shelf 100 Hz, eight bells log-spaced 160 Hz-9 kHz, high shelf 12 kHz, Q 0.8, gains only
candidate.chosen_on: target fit over 4 development passages (indices 0, 13, 26, 39), excluded below

predefined_rules.equivalence: final response within 0.25 dB of today's on every case; failed on the development passages because today's fitter itself misses its target by up to ~0.5 dB
predefined_rules.rule_7b: same failure and recommendation status on every case; target RMS error <= today's + 0.05 dB on every case and lower on average; largest correction <= today's + 0.25 dB

cases.composition: 44 cross-take passages x 5 targets x 2 modes x 4 smoothing; their -1 dBFS versions; 4 invalid captures; 20 fit-split harness captures x 5 targets

results.worst_area: Warm target with Broad smoothing (fixed grid 0.22 vs 0.10 dB RMS)

limitations: Target fit measures closeness to the intended curve, not perceptual quality.
Recommendation status depends on band placement, so a different layout can flip apply/reduced.
